title: Web server logs with grep, awk, sort and uniq
audience: a visual learner who finished K-GEN01 (pipes, cut, sort, uniq, grep, awk basics)
focus: reading a web server access log: find the busiest clients, count status codes, find missing pages, and spot a client that keeps failing to log in

data.access.log: web server access log in the combined format, 300 lines, one request per line. Whitespace-separated fields: $1 client IP, $4 start of the timestamp such as [26/Nov/2026:09:00:15, $6 the quoted method such as "GET, $7 the path, $9 the HTTP status code, $10 the response size in bytes.

lab_questions: which client IPs made the most requests (top 5)
how many requests per status code, most common first
which client has repeated 401 or 403 answers on /login or /admin
how many requests per hour (the hour is in field 4)
avoid: any attack technique: this page is about reading logs and spotting patterns only
